name: Fuse-and-Refine Integration into DepthSplat
text:
# Fuse-and-Refine Integration into DepthSplat
Also called: DepthSplat + Ours

## Overview
This method integrates the "Fuse-and-Refine" module into the [DepthSplat](#18278-depthsplat.md) framework to improve feed-forward novel view synthesis. It addresses the limitation of standard DepthSplat by enhancing feature aggregation and refinement, resulting in higher fidelity [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) reconstructions from sparse input views. It distinguishes itself from the base DepthSplat implementation by adding a specific fusion and refinement stage that boosts metrics like PSNR and LPIPS, and from sibling methods like 4DGS and [GS-LRM](#1483-gs-lrm.md) by offering superior performance when evaluated under identical sparse-view constraints [S1].

## How it works
**Inputs and Outputs:**
*   **Inputs:** A set of $N$ input images (typically $N=2$ for training, $N=4$ for evaluation) and their corresponding camera poses.
*   **Outputs:** A set of 3D Gaussians (position, covariance, opacity, [spherical harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md) coefficients) suitable for [rasterization](#15310-rasterization.md) via DepthSplat.

**Data Structures:**
The method builds upon the DepthSplat architecture. The core addition is the Fuse-and-Refine module. Specific internal tensor layouts for this module are not detailed in the provided sources, other than the output resolution being compatible with the downstream DepthSplat pipeline [S1].

**Steps:**
1.  **Base Feature Extraction:** The input images are processed by the DepthSplat backbone to extract initial features.
2.  **Fuse-and-Refine Integration:** The Fuse-and-Refine module is inserted into the DepthSplat pipeline. This module aggregates and refines the extracted features to produce a more robust representation for [Gaussian parameter prediction](#18303-gaussian-parameter-prediction.md). [G] The exact internal mechanism of the Fuse-and-Refine module (e.g., attention heads, convolutional layers) is not specified in the provided notes, but it is described as a distinct module that improves upon the baseline [S1].
3.  **Gaussian Parameter Prediction:** The refined features are used to predict the 3D Gaussian parameters (mean, covariance, opacity, color).
4.  **Rasterization:** The predicted Gaussians are rasterized using the DepthSplat renderer to generate novel views.

**Parameters:**
*   **Training Resolution:** $128 \times 192$ pixels [S1].
*   **Training Data:** Subset of the DL3DV dataset, consisting of 1,000 scenes [S1].
*   **Input Views (Training):** 2 views per scene [S1].
*   **Input Views (Evaluation):** 4 views per scene [S1].
*   **Test Scenes:** 10 scenes [S1].

**Edge Cases and Pitfalls:**
*   **Resolution:** The method was evaluated at a reduced resolution ($128 \times 192$). Performance at higher resolutions is not given in the sources [S1].
*   **Generalization:** The method is evaluated on generalization from 2 input views to 4 input views. Performance on other view counts is not given [S1].

## Subtopics

### [Multi-View Feature Extraction Pipeline](22858-multi-view-feature-extraction-pipeline.md)
The [Multi-View Feature Extraction Pipeline](#22858-multi-view-feature-extraction-pipeline.md) aggregates geometry-aware features from multiple input views to produce a unified low-resolution feature tensor.

## Operating characteristics
**Time and Memory Complexity:**
Not given in the sources.

**Measured Performance:**
Evaluated on the DL3DV dataset (10 test scenes, 4 input views) after retraining on a subset (1,000 scenes, 2 input views) at $128 \times 192$ resolution [S1]. The integration of the Fuse-and-Refine module into DepthSplat yields the following improvements over the baseline DepthSplat:
*   **PSNR:** Increases from 16.57 to 17.66 [S1].
*   **LPIPS:** Decreases from 0.4272 to 0.4019 [S1].
*   **LPIS:** Increases from 0.4108 to 0.4426 [S1].

**Strengths and Limitations:**
*   **Strengths:** Significantly outperforms baselines like 4DGS and GS-LRM in feed-forward novel view synthesis tasks [S1].
*   **Limitations:** The provided evaluation is limited to a specific dataset (DL3DV), resolution ($128 \times 192$), and view configuration (2 to 4 views). Performance on other datasets or resolutions is not given [S1].

## Background
The Fuse-and-Refine module was proposed in the paper "Learning Efficient Fuse-and-Refine for [Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting](#9932-feed-forward-3d-gaussian-splatting.md)" [S1]. The authors validated the generalization capability of this module by integrating it into the publicly available DepthSplat implementation [S1]. The method is designed for feed-forward novel view synthesis, aiming to improve the quality of 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) reconstructions from sparse input views.

## Sources
[S1] Learning Efficient Fuse-and-Refine for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting, https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14698v2, fetched 2026-10-27
